title: Inside the test message
payload: The lab highlights 0x4E 0x51: 01001110 01010001 (NQ) inside an opaque upper-interface frame. These two payload bytes are not the whole Ethernet frame. The displayed order is most-significant-bit first within each highlighted byte, a teaching convention for this view.
model: Our declared toy mapping uses −3 → 00, −1 → 01, +1 → 10 and +3 → 11. Positions are zero-based ordinals in the supplied order, not time. One symbol represents two bits here; this is not a complete PAM4 PHY, a voltage scale or a bitrate/throughput calculation.
comparison: Compare the recovered bits with the known laboratory pattern. This comparison is not universal Layer 1 error detection or Ethernet FCS validation. A matching highlighted pattern does not prove the whole route or any higher-layer service.
impairment: A failed length check does not predict damaged bits. Only an explicitly declared toy substitution can show a changed sample. Without that separate trace, received symbols and recovered bits are unknown.
premises: This controlled bench separately declares compatible endpoints, medium and terminations; continuous required conductors; endpoint power; other physical conditions; and upper dependencies known good for this lab. The length result measures length only and does not establish those premises.
overview: The seven realms are a conceptual teaching map. Application meaning, representation, conversations, transport, networking and link framing provide context above physical signals. Real stacks group these functions differently; we do not invent seven mandatory wire headers. The upper realms below are future content, with no playable higher-layer simulation here.

sources.title: ITU-T X.200, 7.7
sources.claim: Physical entities transmit bits over physical media; conceptual architecture, not a universal numeric PHY.

sources.title: RFC 1122, 1.1.3
sources.claim: The Internet suite groups application, transport, Internet and link functions differently from the seven teaching realms.

sources.title: Altera AN 835, 4.2.3 — Clock and Data Recovery
sources.claim: High-speed serial reception includes clock/data recovery. Our explicit discrete sample positions do not implement CDR, analog jitter or a timing reflex challenge. The exact toy map is authored in PROFILE-SYMBOLS, not taken from this source.
